title: Vital Statistics: Census, Civil Registration, NFHS, ICD, and Life Tables

steps.title: Census: the decennial backbone
steps.tx: The **Census of India** counts every person every ten years (last full count 2011) through houselisting then population enumeration under the Census Act 1948, yielding age, sex, literacy, occupation, migration, and household amenities down to village level. It supplies denominators for rates, sampling frames for surveys, and delimitation data for governance, remaining irreplaceable despite its decade long silences.
steps.say: The census counts everyone every ten years. Its village level denominators anchor every rate and survey frame.

steps.title: Civil registration of births and deaths
steps.tx: The **Registration of Births and Deaths Act 1969** (amended since to strengthen digital systems) obliges reporting of every birth and death to the local registrar (twenty one days conventionally, now with online portals), issuing certificates that unlock schooling, inheritance, and insurance. Completeness has climbed above ninety percent for births nationally, converting registration from legal ritual into a live statistical system.
steps.say: Every birth and death must be registered with the local registrar. Certificates serve the family; completeness serves statistics.

steps.title: Medical certification of cause of death
steps.tx: Registered deaths gain statistical value only with the **medical certification of cause of death (MCCD)**: the treating doctor records the causal chain (immediate cause, antecedent causes, underlying cause) in the international form, and coders assign the underlying cause for mortality statistics. Coverage and quality lag behind registration counts, so garbage codes (senility, heart failure as underlying cause) still blunt Indian mortality data.
steps.say: Cause certification turns a death count into mortality intelligence. The underlying cause, not the final event, gets coded.

steps.title: Sample Registration System revisited
steps.tx: Between censuses the **Sample Registration System** dual records births and deaths continuously in sampled units (a resident enumerator plus independent half yearly survey, unmatched events verified), producing annual state level birth, death, infant mortality, and fertility rates. Its cause of death arm uses verbal autopsy (RHIME method) to assign causes where medical certification is absent, powering India's mortality cause estimates.
steps.say: Dual recording fills the census gap with annual rates. Verbal autopsy supplies causes where doctors never certified.

steps.title: National Family Health Survey
steps.tx: The **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)** interviews households and measures biomarkers (haemoglobin, blood pressure, glucose, anthropometry) in rounds (NFHS five in 2019 to 2021), delivering fertility, nutrition, anaemia, immunisation, and disease prevalence by district. Unlike registration systems it measures what families actually experience (stunting thirty five point five percent, wasting nineteen point three percent in NFHS five), including the unregistered.
steps.say: NFHS measures bodies, not just records: anaemia, stunting, pressure, and glucose by district. It catches what registers miss.

steps.title: ICD: classifying diseases and deaths
steps.tx: The **International Classification of Diseases (ICD)** codes every diagnosis and cause of death into standard chapters so mortality and morbidity compare across places and decades; ICD ten served a generation, and ICD eleven (digital, stem plus extension codes) is rolling out. Coding the underlying cause by ICD rules, not local habit, is what makes a district's malaria deaths comparable with a nation's.
steps.say: ICD coding standardises causes worldwide. ICD eleven now succeeds ICD ten with digital stem and extension codes.

steps.title: Notification and HMIS flows
steps.tx: Legally dangerous diseases flow through **notification of infectious diseases** (cholera, plague, and listed conditions under state public health acts and the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme), while routine service data (deliveries, immunisations, outpatients) flow monthly through the Health Management Information System portal from facility to nation. Notification is immediate and case based; HMIS is periodic and aggregate, and confusing their purposes corrupts outbreak response.
steps.say: Notify dangerous diseases immediately by case; report routine services monthly in aggregate. Different speeds, different jobs.

steps.title: Life tables and their uses
steps.tx: A **life table** follows a synthetic cohort through current age specific mortality, yielding survivors (lx), deaths, person years, and life expectancy at each age (ex). India life expectancy at birth approaches seventy years. Life tables feed insurance premia, net reproduction rates, years of potential life lost, and the mortality half of burden of disease calculations in every planning office.
steps.say: Life tables turn death rates into life expectancy and survival curves. They also feed reproduction rates and insurance.

steps.title: Morbidity surveys and record linkage
steps.tx: Mortality data miss living illness, so **morbidity measurement** adds periodic surveys (NFHS, National Sample Survey health rounds), disease registries (cancer, stroke), and record linkage joining a person's events across registers by unique identifiers to build incidence and follow up cohorts. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission's ABHA identifier is India's current bet on linkable records, with privacy safeguards as its governing tension.
steps.say: Surveys and registries measure living illness; linkage follows one person across records. ABHA is India's linkage bet.
